root_cause: During the ARM64 cross-compilation build, three translation units in the openvino_shape_inference target failed to compile because the precompiled header cmake_pch.hxx.gch used by that CMake target is not a valid PCH for the compiler invocation that consumed it (cc1plus: 'not a PCH file'). Because ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD and CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR are ON, this diagnostic is escalated by -Werror=invalid-pch into a hard build failure. This class of error typically occurs when a stale or partially-written .gch artifact (e.g. left over from sccache/ccache reuse, a concurrent/parallel PCH generation race under -j15, or a toolchain/flags mismatch between the PCH-generating compile and the consuming compile) is picked up instead of being regenerated. The commit under investigation (#38393) only touches src/plugins/intel_gpu graph-optimizer code and its unit tests; it does not touch src/core/shape_inference or PCH/cmake configuration, so the failure is very unlikely to be caused by the PR's own diff and looks like an ARM64-cross-compile build-environment/toolchain issue (stale PCH artifact or a PCH-generation race under CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=15) rather than a code regression.
reproduction_steps: Not directly reproducible from a clean checkout without the exact runner image/cache state. To attempt reproduction: use the ARM64 cross-compilation Docker image (openvinogithubactions.azurecr.io/ov_build/ubuntu_22_04_arm64_cross_compilation:pr-38160), configure with the same cmake-options (-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/arm64.toolchain.cmake -DENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON), then run `cmake --build openvino_build --parallel 15` and check whether src/core/shape_inference/CMakeFiles/openvino_shape_inference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch is regenerated cleanly before being consumed by the dependent .cpp.o compiles.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Linux (Ubuntu 22.04, ARM64 cross-compilation, Python 3.11)' workflow; if it passes on rerun, this confirms a transient/stale build-cache or PCH-generation race rather than a code regression.

If the failure recurs, inspect whether sccache is caching PCH compiler invocations (CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache with ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD/PCH) and whether a partially-written or previous-run .gch is being reused across build directories/containers.

Consider adding an explicit dependency/ordering safeguard so all dependent objects wait for a fully-written cmake_pch.hxx.gch before compiling, or temporarily disable ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD for the openvino_shape_inference target on this configuration if the race persists.
Verify sccache is not caching precompiled-header compiler invocations incorrectly for this compiler/arch combination (aarch64-linux-gnu-g++ with -Winvalid-pch).
prevention_strategies: Ensure PCH artifacts are always freshly generated per build (avoid caching .gch files across build directories or sccache keys), and consider not escalating -Werror=invalid-pch to a hard failure for PCH-consuming targets on cross-compilation configurations until the underlying cache/race is fixed, since a stale PCH should trigger a full regeneration rather than fail the whole build.
historical_context: No prior post-commit investigation in this doctor's database references PCH, invalid-pch, or cmake_pch failures; this is a new failure pattern (first occurrence recorded).
